daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo conducted a reshuffle of 16 cabinet positions on 1 October, replacing senior ministers including the Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal and Security Affairs and Foreign Minister as his administration approaches its second anniversary. The major cabinet reorganization involved both new appointees and rotation of existing officials to different portfolios. PDIP responded by saying that official rotations must answer public demands following Prabowo's seventh reshuffle.

  • The DPR Commission III approved by acclamation Commissioner General Suyudi to replace Listyo Sigit as National Police Chief, with the YLBHI questioning the swift replacement process and lack of public involvement.
  • Former National Police Chief Listyo Sigit, who was the second-longest serving police chief, was appointed Presidential Chief of Staff replacing Dudung Abdulrachman.
  • The DPR Commission II established the composition of its working committee on the Electoral Law bill.
  • Constitutional Court hearings continued examining Vice President Gibran's educational qualifications, with a judge questioning the duration of Gibran's education in Singapore and the former KPU chairman admitting he did not verify Gibran's educational requirements during the 2024 presidential election.
  • The Constitutional Court ejected an expert witness from a hearing related to Gibran after his statements about the election dispute case being illegal.
  • Gus Ipul issued legal notices to three individuals over allegations of money flow at the NU Congress.
  • The Director General of Corrections resigned following the exposure of luxury facilities at Cibinong Prison.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir replaced Sugiono in the cabinet reshuffle, with the new minister stating that Indonesia's foreign policy remains aligned with President Prabowo's direction. Arrmanatha backed Indonesia's bid for a UN Security Council seat. An analyst said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is strengthening protection of Indonesians abroad.

  • Indonesia is seeking support for its bid to join the International Civil Aviation Organization Council.
  • A minister pushed for investment certainty during free trade agreement negotiations with the Gulf Cooperation Council.
  • Indonesia and South Korea deepened cooperation on intellectual property matters.
  • Indonesia called for global action to strengthen food security at an international forum.
  • US sanctions on Iran have affected Indonesian companies according to a news report.

Other

The Ministry of Finance is conducting due diligence on transferring Whoosh debt as the high-speed rail project's financial obligations remain under review. The Deputy Finance Minister confirmed that Rp 37 trillion for KDMP obligations has been placed with state-owned banks. The Directorate General of Taxation is preparing a draft increase in non-taxable income thresholds (PTKP), though the amount has not been disclosed.

  • Tax collection from marketplace sellers came into effect starting today.
  • The National Nutrition Agency activated nutrition posts in remote areas and high-stunting regions starting 2 October.
  • Indonesia has extinguished 3,799 hectares of wildfires across six priority provinces.
  • MRT Jakarta has partnered with a Singaporean investor to develop the Glodok transit-oriented development area.
  • Antam gold prices fell Rp 5,000 to Rp 2.576 million per gram today.
